charts.title: Search and screening funnel
charts.subtitle: Read each block top to bottom: every bar is one step of the pipeline, the number is what was left after it, and the grey note says what that step removed.

charts.title: Landscape saturation
charts.subtitle: Left: products found by the sampled search and the statistical estimate of how many exist (shaded = 95% range). Right: how complete the search looks; the search may stop once both lines clear the target.

charts.title: Competitor crowding by category
charts.subtitle: Each bar counts the verified products in one category; longer bars mean a more crowded market. Colours split each category by how products charge.

charts.title: Demand-supply gap map
charts.subtitle: Each bubble is one job people are trying to get done. Higher = more people asking (weighted by how strong their evidence is); further right = more products already serving it; bigger = more verified quotes. The shaded corner (above-median demand, below-median supply) is where gaps live.

charts.title: Evidence profile
charts.subtitle: Four views of the same quotes: what people said, how strong the evidence is (S0 opinion up to S4 money spent), what kind of page it came from, and which websites supplied it.

charts.title: Evidence over time
charts.subtitle: Each bar counts verified quotes posted in one quarter, split by what they say. The shaded band is the protocol's recency window: quotes inside it describe the market as it is now.

charts.title: Coding reliability
charts.subtitle: Each bar is one code (a job, pain or theme) that two coders applied separately; Krippendorff's alpha of 1 means perfect agreement. Bars past 0.80 are reliable; 0.667-0.80 supports tentative conclusions only.

charts.title: Gap cards scorecard
charts.subtitle: One row per gap idea. The first five columns are the evidence thresholds every idea must pass (green tick = met, red cross = short); the last two say what happened to it.

charts.title: Ranking and sizing
charts.subtitle: Left: the desk score out of 100 (longer = stronger case) and how often the gap stays in the top 3 when the criteria weights are varied. Right: obtainable revenue per year (low to high, dot = base case) against the founder's ambition line.

charts.title: Price ladder
charts.subtitle: Each dot is one product's cheapest paid plan per month (USD); the dark tick and the number on the right are the category median. Cheapest categories at the top. The scale is logarithmic, so equal distances mean equal price ratios.

charts.title: Demand bursts
charts.subtitle: Each panel tracks how often a term appears per month. Shaded spans are bursts the burst test found; orange means statistically significant, grey means it could be chance. Ticks at the bottom mark dated why-now events.

charts.title: Run effort and amendments
charts.subtitle: Left: subagents assigned per pipeline phase, in the order they ran. Right: the running total over the run, with each protocol amendment marked by its number (listed below).
